title: Disentangling the Dual Role of NIC Receive Rings
problem: NIC receive rings simultaneously buffer incoming packets and carry control metadata, creating architectural tensions that reduce efficiency and create performance/functionality conflicts across different workload patterns.
motivation: Network interface optimization directly impacts datacenter throughput and latency, making the design of packet reception mechanisms critical to system performance.
method: The paper characterizes how NIC receive rings handle dual purposes through architectural analysis and measurement, likely proposing hardware or software mechanisms to decouple control and buffering functions for independent optimization.
key_novelty: Formally identifying and separating the conflicting architectural roles within NIC receive rings to enable specialized optimization of each function.
contributions: Characterization of dual-role design tensions in NIC receive ring architecture
Measurement framework demonstrating performance impact of role conflicts
Proposed decoupling mechanism to isolate control and data functions
